environment_features.name: Glacial Origins
environment_features.description: Vashon Island was formed by the retreat of the Vashon Stade of the Fraser Glaciation, the last major ice age in the Puget Sound region (~12,000–10,000 BCE). The island's terrain is composed of glacial till — a mix of clay, sand, gravel, and boulders deposited by the retreating ice sheet. The glaciation carved the deep waterways of Puget Sound that now surround the island.

environment_features.name: Stratigraphy
environment_features.description: The retreating Vashon glacier left a distinctive layered geological profile: - **Vashon Till** (surface): Dense, unsorted mixture of clay, silt, sand, and gravel - **Esperance Sand** (middle): Porous advance outwash deposited by meltwater streams ahead of the glacier - **Lawton Clay** (deep): Fine sediment deposited in proglacial lakes, largely impermeable This layering determines the island's hydrology: water percolates through permeable till and outwash until hitting impermeable clay, emerg...

environment_features.name: Puget Sound Formation
environment_features.description: By approximately 14,000 BCE, glacial retreat opened the Strait of Juan de Fuca, allowing saltwater to re-enter the Puget Sound basin and transforming freshwater proglacial lakes (including Glacial Lake Russell) into a saltwater inland sea. The resulting fjord system averages 450 feet in depth, with a maximum of 930 feet off Jefferson Point. Deep channels surrounding Vashon Island — some as deep as the island is high (over 600 feet) — were carved by subglacial meltwater during the Vashon Stade.

environment_features.name: Terrain
environment_features.description: - **Bluffs:** Steep glacial bluffs line much of the coastline, particularly on the western and northern shores. Formed by erosion exploiting the contrast between permeable and impermeable geological layers. - **Ravines:** Hundreds of small ravines and creek valleys carved through erodible glacial sediments by surface water. Shinglemill Creek and Judd Creek cut entirely through the outwash layer. - **Soils:** Rich glacial soils support agriculture, particularly the clay loam ideal for strawber...

environment_features.name: Post-Glacial Succession
environment_features.description: (~12,000–8,000 BCE) After ice sheet retreat, the bare glacial landscape underwent classic post-glacial ecological succession: 1. **16,000–15,000 BP:** Temperatures ~4°C colder than present; largely barren landscape 2. **14,000–12,000 BP:** Lodgepole pine (*Pinus contorta*) established in open parkland conditions 3. **12,000–10,000 BP:** Wider variety of trees; transition to closed forest with western hemlock and alder 4. **~8,000 BCE:** Signature Pacific Northwest species (Douglas fir, wester...

environment_features.name: Historic Forest Cover
environment_features.description: Before European-American settlement, the island was densely forested with old-growth: - **Douglas fir** (*Pseudotsuga menziesii*) — dominant canopy species - **Western red cedar** (*Thuja plicata*) — culturally significant to Coast Salish peoples; called the "Tree of Life" - **Western hemlock** (*Tsuga heterophylla*) — shade-tolerant understory - **Big-leaf maple** (*Acer macrophyllum*) — in ravines and lowlands - **Red alder** (*Alnus rubra*) — pioneer species in disturbed areas The cedar wa...

environment_features.name: Deforestation & Recovery
environment_features.description: - **1852–1860s:** Early logging camps near shoreline; ox-team skid roads to beach. environment_features.name: Marine Environment
environment_features.description: - **Shoreline:** Mix of rocky beaches, sandy shores, and tidal flats. Vashon carries half of all King County's shorelines. - **Salmon:** All five species of Pacific salmon (Chinook, coho, sockeye, chum, pink) colonized Puget Sound ~14,900 years ago in two pulses — from the south via the Chehalis River and from the north through the Strait of Juan de Fuca. - **Shellfish:** Productive intertidal beds established by ~6,000 BCE, particularly in Quartermaster Harbor. environment_features.name: Agricultural Landscape
environment_features.description: Five distinct phases of agricultural history: 1. **Indigenous stewardship** (pre-contact): Seasonal round of resource gathering — camas root, berries (salal, huckleberry, salmonberry), shellfish, salmon, waterfowl, marine mammals. Fire used to maintain prairie openings. 2. **Homestead era** (1865–1890s): Mixed subsistence farming; clearing forest for fields. 3. **Strawberry era** (1890–1942): Signature crop cultivated primarily by Japanese American families. environment_features.name: Conservation
environment_features.description: - **Vashon-Maury Island Land Trust** (founded 1989): Over 2,000 acres permanently protected, 10 miles of public trails. Preserves include Shinglemill Creek, Judd Creek, Fisher Pond, Christensen Pond, and 12 acres of the historic Matsuda Farm. Programs include "Seven over Seventy" (large private holdings) and "The Four Creeks Campaign" (major watersheds). - **Glacier Northwest Mine Controversy** (1998–2010): Proposed gravel mine expansion on Maury Island (7.5M tons/year) fought by Preserve Our...

environment_features.name: Pacific Maritime
environment_features.description: Vashon Island has a mild, maritime climate moderated by the waters of Puget Sound: - **Winters:** Cool and wet (average January temperature ~40°F / 4°C) - **Summers:** Warm and dry (average July temperature ~65°F / 18°C) - **Precipitation:** ~38 inches annually, concentrated October through March - **Rain shadow:** Partially in the Olympic rain shadow, receiving less rain than areas to the west - **Frost:** Occasional; the maritime influence moderates temperature extremes - **Growing season:*...

environment_features.name: Holocene Climatic Optimum
environment_features.description: (~7,500–2,500 BCE) A prolonged warm period with temperatures averaging ~2°C warmer than the modern baseline and ~45% less precipitation. This expanded prairie-like openings and oak woodland at the expense of dense conifer forest, influenced fire regimes, and affected distribution of plant foods important to early inhabitants. The modern cool, wet climate pattern became established after ~4,200 years ago.
